verdict.reasons: Core product identity is correct, with one clearly identifiable white-and-blue AFP drip-tape carton roll, recognizable genuine AFP and blue water-drop logo, and owner-authorized 'Drip Irrigation Tape' caption. The 'AFP | 09134922013' watermark is present and required. The technical evidence reasonably supports a pressure article: a pressure gauge is attached to a thread port, and a thin drip-tape lateral is connected with a small take-off fitting; the gauge face is angled away without invented readable pressure markings. Crop context contains only neutral seedlings and soil. No people, no additional rolls, no unrelated plumbing substitutes, no collage/split panels, and no contradictory framing. A small visual advisory warning arises from previous image QA feedback noting insufficient caption room on the white sleeve, but the observed text remains legible and coherent in this candidate, so it is treated as a non-blocking note rather than a core defect. Overall score exceeds the minimum 90 threshold.

focused_physical_review.reason: The white-and-blue AFP package is not isolated; the installed irrigation line runs to the package and a separate, distinct loose coil of product (the looped section leading to the gauge) lies on the soil to the right. The required package sits in the soil with loose ground at its base, preventing a clear gap behind it. No white ribbon, strap, or tape tail is protruding from the carton.
